rationale: Meets the preferred position: no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us. Every use of "exclusive" in the Agreement either characterises the licence granted to us as expressly non-exclusive (Preamble; p0030; p0043; p0049; p0050; p0052; p0078) or is unrelated boilerplate (payments "exclusive of" taxes at p0051, exclusive jurisdiction at p0146, entire-agreement at p0155, non-exclusive remedy at p0142). Targeted searches for sole-supplier formulations ("shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure ... from any third party", "competing", "any other platform") returned no results. Article II's "Additional Restrictions" (p0035-p0047) are IP-protective limits on how we may use the Licensed Technology (no sublicensing, transfer, derivative works or reverse engineering) and do not restrict our freedom to license or use a competing FX trading platform; likewise Article VI (p0085) restricts onward transfer of Licensor's technology only. Two points noted rather than flagged under this rule: (i) the non-exclusivity here runs in Licensor's favour (it may license others), which is a limit on our exclusivity rather than an obligation on us, and so is not a deviation under this rule; and (ii) the "Right of First Refusal" in Article XXII (p0139), which the plan hint suggested might be a platform-purchase lock-in, is in fact a ROFR over a sale of substantially all our assets or a merger, i.e. a change-of-control restriction outside the scope of this supply-exclusivity rule (it sits with the change-of-control/assignment rules, together with the consent requirement at p0134).
